summary: Adds a `stash auth login` command (region select, OAuth device-code flow and device-to-keyset binding through the new native dependency @cipherstash/auth 0.34.2) and makes the same flow the first, mandatory step of `stash init`. It also rewrites the shipped README and the init 'next steps' to say local development needs no CS_* environment variables, pins three existing runtime dependencies to exact versions (evlog 1.11.0 to 1.9.0 and @byteslice/result 0.2.2 to 0.2.0 in the lockfile), and is released as a minor bump. Library encryption paths, payloads and exports are not touched. The material risks are in the CLI and its guidance. `stash init` can no longer complete without network access, an interactive region prompt, a browser confirmation and a successful device binding. There is no skip or 'already authenticated' check, and a failure aborts before any scaffolding. The new guidance that no env vars are needed contradicts code that is unchanged at head: `stash secrets` still exits unless CS_WORKSPACE_CRN, CS_CLIENT_ID and CS_CLIENT_KEY are set, and LockContext still requires CS_WORKSPACE_CRN or cipherstash.toml. No test covers any CLI code, and no CI results were provided. Failures are loud onboarding failures with no data or encryption effect, so the impact is medium.

behaviour_changes.description: New CLI command `stash auth login`: an interactive region selection, then the device-code flow (opens a browser, polls for a token that @cipherstash/auth persists to ~/.cipherstash/auth.json per the CLI message), then binding the device to the default keyset. Unknown subcommands exit 1.

`stash init` now runs authenticateStep before every other step, unconditionally. It has no flag to skip it and does not check for an existing token. A rejected token poll propagates to main() as a fatal exit 1. A failed bind calls process.exit(1). Both happen before connection selection, schema generation or forge install.

Running init or auth login now creates or overwrites a user-level token file (~/.cipherstash/auth.json, written by @cipherstash/auth) and registers or binds the device with the default keyset in the selected region on the CipherStash service.

The shipped README and the init next-steps output no longer tell users to create an account and set CS_* credentials. The README says local development needs no environment variables or credential files, and that the SDK and CLI use the saved token. The TOML config documentation was removed.

New runtime dependency @cipherstash/auth 0.34.2 with per-platform native optional packages (same six platforms as protect-ffi 0.21.0). @byteslice/result, evlog and uuid are changed from caret ranges to exact pins. The lockfile resolution for packages/stack moves evlog 1.11.0 to 1.9.0 and @byteslice/result 0.2.2 to 0.2.0.

failure_scenarios.title: `stash init` cannot complete without interactive, networked device login and a successful keyset bind
failure_scenarios.trigger: A user runs `npx stash init` offline, behind a proxy, in a non-interactive or CI shell, in a region not in the hard-coded list, lets the device code expire, or the bind call fails (e.g. the account has no default keyset). Re-running init also forces a new login and bind every time.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: STEPS now starts with authenticateStep (init/index.ts:16-22). It always calls selectRegion, login and bindDevice (steps/authenticate.ts:7-11) and does not check for an existing token. Rejections from beginDeviceCodeFlow or pollForToken are not caught in login() (auth/login.ts:30-51) or in initCommand, which only handles CancelledError (init/index.ts:46-52). They reach main()'s catch and exit 1 (stash.ts:93-97). A failed bindClientDevice calls process.exit(1) (auth/login.ts:57-64).
failure_scenarios.consequence: Init exits before connection selection, schema generation and forge install. At base, init worked with no account or network. Users get no scaffolding and no fallback path. Onboarding is blocked for any user who cannot complete the device flow or bind.

failure_scenarios.title: New guidance says no env vars are needed for local development, but `stash secrets` and LockContext still require them
failure_scenarios.trigger: A user follows the updated README or init next-steps: they run `stash auth login`, set no CS_* variables and no cipherstash.toml, then use `stash secrets ...` or `LockContext`.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: The README now says no environment variables or credential files are needed and that the CLI uses ~/.cipherstash/auth.json (README.md:451, 495-497). Init next-steps dropped the instruction to set CS_* (providers/base.ts:13-14 head vs base). At head, secrets/helpers.ts getConfig still exits 1 when CS_WORKSPACE_CRN, CS_CLIENT_ID or CS_CLIENT_KEY is missing (helpers.ts:33-51). LockContext calls loadWorkSpaceId(), which throws without CS_WORKSPACE_CRN or cipherstash.toml (identity/index.ts:62, utils/config/index.ts:59-71). This change removed the TOML documentation.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Shipped docs and CLI output tell users something the code does not support. The secrets CLI and identity-aware encryption fail on first use with 'missing environment variables' or 'workspace CRN' errors. No data effect, but onboarding guidance is wrong in a published README.
missing_verification: An end-to-end run of the documented local-dev path (auth login, then secrets set, then LockContext) with no CS_* variables set
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Make the secrets CLI and loadWorkSpaceId fall back to the device token or profile, or scope the README claim to what actually works and keep the CS_* and cipherstash.toml instructions for the secrets CLI and identity.

failure_scenarios.title: Encryption() may fail after following the new 'no credentials' quick start if protect-ffi 0.21.0 does not read the device token
failure_scenarios.trigger: A user completes `stash init` (device login) and calls `Encryption({ schemas })` with no CS_* variables set, as the README now says is enough.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: Encryption.init passes only the explicit config to protect-ffi newClient and relies on its internal env fallback (encryption/index.ts:79-90). This change does not bump protect-ffi (still 0.21.0). The repository contains nothing showing that newClient reads ~/.cipherstash/auth.json, and the package contents were not available to check.
failure_scenarios.consequence: If newClient does not support the token, every new user following the quick start gets a ClientInitError when creating the client. The README examples would fail at the first step of the documented path.
missing_verification: Confirm that protect-ffi 0.21.0 newClient resolves credentials from the @cipherstash/auth token store
A smoke test: device login, then Encryption() with an empty env
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Verify the protect-ffi credential chain before publishing. If it does not support the token, bump protect-ffi or keep the CS_* instructions for SDK use.

failure_scenarios.title: Library consumers silently get older evlog and @byteslice/result versions with exact pins
failure_scenarios.trigger: A consumer installs the new @cipherstash/stack minor release.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: The dependency ranges become exact pins (package.json:208-215). The lockfile resolution moves evlog 1.11.0 to 1.9.0 and @byteslice/result 0.2.2 to 0.2.0. The logger only imports initLogger and createRequestLogger (utils/logger/index.ts:1). evlog was introduced at 1.9.0 in commit ac17968, which lowers the chance of a missing API.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Probably benign. At worst, logging behaviour differs from the version CI previously resolved, and consumers get duplicate copies of these packages. The repository's tests at head will now run against 1.9.0.

evidence.claim: authenticateStep always runs selectRegion, login and bindDevice, with no token-exists check or skip.
authenticateStep is first in STEPS. initCommand only handles CancelledError and rethrows everything else.
login() awaits beginDeviceCodeFlow and pollForToken with no error handling. The success message says the token is saved to ~/.cipherstash/auth.json.
bindDevice calls process.exit(1) when bindClientDevice fails.
Regions are a hard-coded list (TODO to pull from the API). Region selection is an interactive prompt, and cancelling exits 0.
The auth command is dispatched from main(). Uncaught errors print 'Fatal error' and exit 1.
The README says no environment variables or credentials are needed for local development and that the SDK and CLI use ~/.cipherstash/auth.json. CS_* is only for production.
The `stash auth` section says no environment variables or credential files are needed for local development.
The secrets CLI getConfig still requires CS_WORKSPACE_CRN, CS_CLIENT_ID and CS_CLIENT_KEY and exits 1 if any is missing.
loadWorkSpaceId throws without CS_WORKSPACE_CRN or cipherstash.toml. LockContext calls it (identity/index.ts:62).
At base, init next-steps told users to create an account and set the CS_* variables. At head, this was replaced by the forge setup step only.
The diff removes the TOML config section (cipherstash.toml / cipherstash.secret.toml) and the note that the CLI reads CS_* variables.
Adds @cipherstash/auth 0.34.2, pins @byteslice/result, evlog and uuid exactly, and leaves protect-ffi at 0.21.0.
The collector reports the dependency changes: @cipherstash/auth added and three caret ranges replaced by exact versions.
